coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 1
record.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope up to 180 ft (188 ft on the enacted height map, taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count), one of three blocks (with 5 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage; no design review approval or construction start found. The amended and restated development agreement, which includes Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'); its effect on Block 1's timing has not been read.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to an Assessor parcel of its own: it lies entirely inside active Assessor lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, added to DataSF's Assessor layer on 2024-10-15), a larger lot that is not Block 1's own. No source read describes the block's ground condition. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram by fitting it to multiple real street points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with control-point georeferencing. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) in a single consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after a mis-measured control point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. The statement that the block is unbuilt is not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) does not list a Block 1 application. The statement that the diagram is dated 2020 is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The whole block lies inside active Assessor lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, added 2024-10-15), a larger lot that has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is our own reading of the parcel data, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, PDF p.107) says 'Within the PG&E sub-area are a portion of Block 1, the entirety of Blocks 13 and 14', and defines that sub-area as 'a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018'. That describes ownership in 2018: DataSF now lists lot 4175018 as retired (2024-10-15, the date lots 4175499 and 4175500 were added).
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 1, marked '1*' (a potential district parking garage location up to 90 ft in height and potential grocery store location), in two height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: '180'/85'' on its west part (maximum height 180 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and '85'' on its east part. The '115'MAX' marking on the figure is a plan-dimension line for the tower zone, not a height. The October 7, 2020 Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment approval places Block 1 in Phase 2 and moves the option for space for a Public Library to Block 1 in Phase 2 (an option, not a committed branch). No construction-start source found.

changes.text: The schedule note for Block 1 still quoted the City's earlier listing (final action October 6, 2026, status 'Mayors Office'). The Legistar page now lists the agreement as passed, final action and enactment October 13, 2026 (Enactment No. 208-26), and the note says so. open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 1; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

No source found claiming a specific planned use (e.g., grocery store) beyond the D4D's own generic 'Potential District Parking Garage Location, Potential Grocery Store Location' asterisk notation, which applies to Blocks 1, 5 and 13 collectively, not to Block 1 alone.

Block-specific schedule: the only one read is the 2020 forecast in SocketSite's table (Block 1 vertical development 2029-2031, Phase 2); no design review approval for Block 1 was found. BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated Development Agreement, including amendments to its Phasing Plan; passed on first reading Sept 29, 2026; Legistar lists it enacted Oct 13, 2026) may change the phasing; the Sept 28, 2026 draft agreement attached to it (Exhibit M-1 Phasing Plan) gives no calendar year for Block 1, so no newer Block 1 date was found and the expected 2031 completion is a 2020 phase forecast only.
